title: Confocal measurement of microplastics uptake by plants
author: Li, Luo, et al.

steps.title: Label polystyrene beads
steps.instruction: Prepare polystyrene (PS) microbeads of the desired diameters (0.2 μm, 2.0 μm, 5.0 μm, 7.0 μm) and label them with the two fluorescent markers: Nile blue (red fluorescence) and 4‑chloro‑7‑nitro‑1,2,3‑benzoxadiazole (green fluorescence).

steps.title: Prepare control and treatment solutions
steps.instruction: Make Hoagland hydroponic solution as the growth medium. For controls, use Hoagland solution without any fluorescent PS beads. For treatments, add PS bead suspensions to Hoagland solution at the following concentrations: 0.5 mg L⁻¹, 5.0 mg L⁻¹, and 50.0 mg L⁻¹ for 0.2 μm beads; and 50.0 mg L⁻¹ for each of the larger bead sizes (2.0 μm, 5.0 μm, 7.0 μm).

steps.title: Grow wheat seedlings hydroponically
steps.instruction: Place wheat seedlings in the prepared Hoagland solutions, ensuring separate containers for each bead size and concentration as well as for the untreated control.

steps.title: Expose plants to beads
steps.instruction: Maintain the seedlings in the respective bead‑containing Hoagland solutions for 10 days under standard growth conditions.

steps.title: Harvest and section plant tissues
steps.instruction: After 10 days, collect roots, stems, and leaves. Prepare longitudinal sections of the mature root zone and cross‑sections of root, stem, and leaf tissues. For root sections, sample the zone 70 mm from the root apex. Mount sections for microscopy.

steps.title: Set microscope detector gain
steps.instruction: Adjust the confocal laser scanning microscope (CLSM) detector gain using images from the untreated control plants (which show no autofluorescence at the specific excitation) and then lock the gain at that setting for all subsequent image acquisitions.

steps.title: Acquire confocal images
steps.instruction: Capture images of each tissue section using the CLSM under identical settings: acquire bright‑field images and fluorescence images in the red channel (Nile blue) and green channel (4‑chloro‑7‑nitro‑1,2,3‑benzoxadiazole). Record merged bright‑field/confocal images. Use a scale bar of 100 μm for all images.

steps.title: Analyze fluorescence distribution
steps.instruction: Compare fluorescence intensity across the different bead concentrations and sizes. Note concentration‑dependent fluorescence in roots for 0.2 μm beads (0.5–50 mg L⁻¹). Record significant fluorescence in roots, shoots, and leaves for 0.2 μm beads, few signals for 2.0 μm beads, and almost none for 5.0 μm and 7.0 μm beads. Observe aggregates of 0.2 μm beads in the xylem and cortex, indicating apoplastic transport, and track bead movement from roots to stems and leaves via the vascular system. Confirm absence of fluorescence in stems and leaves for 2.0 μm beads.
